physics_goals.note: First goal from the INSPIRE long name 'A Study of CP Violation in B Meson Decays'; the third is derived from the experiment's published result programme.
physics_goals.quote: The Belle detector was designed and constructed to carry out quantitative studies of rare B-meson decay modes with very small branching fractions using an asymmetric e + e − collider operating at the ϒ(4S) resonance, the KEK-B-factory.
value: Study CP violation in B-meson decays and test the Kobayashi-Maskawa mechanism
Measure rare B decays with small branching fractions
Study charm and tau physics and charmonium(-like) spectroscopy

summary.plain: An experiment at the KEK laboratory in Japan that ran from 1999 to 2010. It watched electrons and positrons collide to make pairs of B particles, and showed that matter and antimatter behave differently — work that led to the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.
summary.technical: B-factory experiment at the asymmetric-energy KEKB e⁺e⁻ collider running at the Υ(4S); >1 ab⁻¹ recorded, establishing time-dependent CP violation in B⁰ decays, evidence for D⁰-D⁰bar mixing and B⁻→τ⁻ν, and the discovery of the X(3872).

unique_capabilities.note: Derived from the detector paper's statement of purpose; no source consulted lists 'unique capabilities' in these words.
unique_capabilities.quote: Such studies require data samples containing ~10 7 B-meson decays.
value: Asymmetric-energy e⁺e⁻ collisions at the Υ(4S) giving a boosted B–B̄ system for time-dependent CP-violation measurements
Clean, kinematically constrained B-meson pair production with a known initial state
